definition: Residual connections, or shortcuts, help to avoid the vanishing gradient problem in deep networks by allowing gradients to flow through a shortcut path.
details: Residual connections, or shortcuts, help to avoid the vanishing gradient problem in deep networks by allowing gradients to flow through a shortcut path. They are used extensively in deep residual networks (ResNets).

explainer.lead: Residual connections let a network pass information and gradients straight past a block, which is what makes very deep networks trainable at all. Without them, gradients shrink as they propagate through many layers and learning stalls.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a staircase with a side ramp at every step: if a step is hard to climb, you can take the ramp instead, so you keep moving instead of getting stuck.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers insert the shortcut into blocks as x + f(x), often with a projection when input and output shapes differ. A common pitfall is mismatched dimensions or loss of the shortcut if a nonlinearity is applied on the shortcut path.
tiers.paperLevel: The motif is x ↦ f(x) + x, where f is an arbitrary neural network module. Its known function is to allow gradients to flow through a shortcut path, mitigating the vanishing gradient problem in deep networks; the definition does not guarantee performance on its own.

explainer.example: A block computes f(x) with two stacked layers and adds the original input x, so the layer output feeds forward and the input is carried around it.
